source: RI-STL01 §7. RI-AI01 T04/T06 give the skeleton (walk to last-known-position; leash after 12 s in SEARCH) and are NOT re-opened; these four behaviours sit on top.

s1.name: Last-known-position, then the plausible set
s1.spec: The searcher walks to LKP, then visits up to 3 nav-mesh cover volumes within 8 m of LKP, in order of 'reachable from LKP without crossing the searcher's own cone' — i.e. it checks WHERE YOU COULD HAVE GONE, not random points.
s1.order: nearest first, ties broken by volume id — deterministic and independently recomputable from the nav mesh

s2.name: Escalating radius
s2.spec: Search radius grows 8 m -> 14 m -> 20 m across the 12 s, then leashes. A player who hides at 10 m and holds still is found; one who keeps moving away is not. Holding still is not a universal answer.

s3.name: Propagation, bounded
s3.spec: On entering SEARCH, a searcher raises every ally within 12 m to alert 45 — below SUSPICIOUS, so the room gets TWITCHY without the whole level aggroing. One hop only, never chains.

s4.name: The zone remembers
s4.spec: After any SEARCH that ends without acquisition, the zone's baseline alert for all its NPCs is set to 25 for 180 s, and civilians' contextWeight for that zone is x1.4 for 20 in-game minutes. Extinguished lights are relit; opened doors are closed; a moved body is found. This survives leaving and re-entering the zone, and it survives death and save.
s4.ingame_minute_note: The world clock runs at 30x, so one in-game minute is 2 real seconds; 20 in-game minutes is 40 s of play and 2,400 f@60. If W1-02's day/night piece sets a different ratio this constant moves with it and nothing else changes.
s4.why_it_is_here: It is the single behaviour that makes a botched infiltration cost something after the immediate danger passes. Without it, being spotted costs you the next thirty seconds and nothing more, so the optimal stealth play is to blunder forward and wait out the search — which is neither tense nor Morrowind.
